extent:
Four liturgies: Palm Sunday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday of Holy Week. Within
them this tracer claims only the units it lists. It says nothing about the
Ordinary, the Canon, the chants' notation, the ceremonies not reduced to a text
unit here, the Office, or Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Holy Week. Silence in
this file is silence because nothing was established, never because the state
was checked and found unchanged: guidance/recensions.md Rule 4.

lines.label: Roman typical editions
lines.note: The line Quo primum established and every act that revised it.

lines.label: Uses exempted by Quo primum
lines.note:
Quo primum did not abolish every other use. It excepted those whose institution
was approved by the Apostolic See or whose custom had been kept above two hundred
years, and said of them in terms that it took their manner of celebrating away by
no means. Those uses -- among them the Ambrosian, the Lyonese, and the uses of
the Dominicans, Carmelites and Carthusians -- kept their own Holy Week and never
returned to this line. This tracer holds no witness for any of them, so the line
has its birth act and nothing after it. An empty branch that is honestly empty
is the point: the fork is in the record because an act put it there, and its
emptiness measures what this corpus holds, not what happened.

stations.citation: Pius V, Quo primum tempore, 14 July 1570, printed in the front matter of the witnesses below.
stations.effect: Establishes the state this tracer treats as its base.
stations.title: Quo primum promulgates the Missale Romanum

stations.citation: Pius V, Quo primum tempore, 14 July 1570, exempting clause.
stations.effect:
Creates the parallel lines. Nothing in this tracer attaches to it, because no
witness to any exempted use is in this corpus.
stations.instrument: Apostolic constitution Quo primum tempore, exempting clause
stations.title: Quo primum excepts the uses above two hundred years old

stations.citation: Clement VIII, Cum sanctissimum Eucharistiae sacramentum, 7 July 1604.
stations.effect: No departure in this slice has been established for it.
stations.instrument: Apostolic constitution Cum sanctissimum Eucharistiae sacramentum
stations.title: Clement VIII issues the emended Missal

stations.citation: Urban VIII, Si quid est in rebus humanis, 2 September 1634.
stations.effect: No departure in this slice has been established for it.
stations.instrument: Apostolic constitution Si quid est in rebus humanis
stations.title: Urban VIII issues the further emended Missal

stations.citation: Pius X, Divino afflatu, 1 November 1911, cited by name in the 1920 decree of approbation.
stations.title: Divino afflatu orders the new arrangement of the Psalter

stations.citation: Pius X, Abhinc duos annos, 23 October 1913, cited by name in the 1920 decree of approbation.
stations.title: Abhinc duos annos orders the calendar's revision

stations.authority: Benedict XV, through the Sacred Congregation of Rites
stations.citation: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Decretum approbationis editionis typicae Vaticanae, printed at the head of the 1920 Missale Romanum; the corpus records the promulgation as 25 July 1920.
stations.effect: No departure in this slice has been established for it.
stations.title: The Vatican typical edition of 1920 is approved

stations.citation: Sacred Congregation of Rites, De rubricis ad simpliciorem formam redigendis, 23 March 1955, named and dated in Rubricarum instructum.
stations.instrument: Decretum generale De rubricis ad simpliciorem formam redigendis
stations.title: The rubrics are reduced to a simpler form

stations.authority: Pius XII, through the Sacred Congregation of Rites
stations.citation: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Maxima redemptionis nostrae mysteria, 16 November 1955, in Acta Apostolicae Sedis 47 (1955), with the accompanying Instruction.
stations.effect: The largest set of departures in this slice: see the departures keyed to this act.
stations.title: Maxima redemptionis restores the order of Holy Week

stations.citation: John XXIII, Rubricarum instructum, 25 July 1960, printed in the front matter of the 1962 witness.
stations.effect: No departure in this slice; it approves the code, which the next act promulgates.
stations.instrument: Apostolic letter motu proprio Rubricarum instructum
stations.title: Rubricarum instructum approves the new body of rubrics

stations.citation: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Decretum generale, 26 July 1960, printed in the front matter of the 1962 witness.
stations.effect: Renames the Introit in every mass of this slice for which a unit was read.
stations.instrument: Decretum generale quo novus rubricarum Breviarii ac Missalis Romani codex promulgatur
stations.title: The Code of Rubrics is promulgated

stations.authority: John XXIII, through the Sacred Congregation of Rites
stations.citation: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Novo rubricarum corpore, 23 June 1962, printed in the front matter of the Vatican typical edition, at page 2 of the CMAA facsimile registered as artifact.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.cmaa-facsimile-pdf.
stations.effect: Carries the 1955 reform into the typical edition.
stations.instrument: Decree Novo rubricarum corpore, promulgating the typical edition of the Missale Romanum of 1962
stations.title: The 1962 typical edition carries the reform and the new code
